item.title: Open Playful Pedagogy Workshop - Role Play Across Disciplines — Tue Oct 27, 12:00 PM — None
item.description:

item.title: m6A-mediated Control of Gene Expression — Tue Oct 27, 12:30 PM — Nanaline Duke 147
item.description:

Most work in the lab investigates the highly abundant RNA chemical modification m6A and how it impacts RNA expression in diverse cell types, including within the nervous system.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Build a Custom Chatbot — Tue Oct 27, 1:00 PM — The TEC - Technology Engagement Center
item.description:
This class teaches the fundamentals of building custom AI chatbots. We'll start with core large language model (LLM) concepts including how models process information (context windows, tokens), differences between model types (reasoning vs. non-reasoning, open vs. closed source), and key constraints that shape chatbot design. From there, we'll cover system prompt design (how to shape behavior and personality) and extending capabilities through tools and knowledge retrieval. Using Duke's AI infrastructure, attendees will gain hands-on experience building chatbots tailored to specific domains or tasks. Come prepared with ideas for chatbots that could support your own workflows!
Source: Duke University

I'll also point out differences between Affinity and Illustrator and PowerPoint along the way for those transferring skills. There are no prerequisites. This event is open to non-Duke participants.

item.title: Black Market Intimacies: The Transpacific Sexual Economy of the Korean War — Tue Oct 27, 3:00 PM — Rubenstein Library Carpenter Conference Room 249
item.description:
"Black Market Intimacies" reveals how illicit exchanges of money and commodities involving sexual encounters between Korean and Japanese women and US soldiers provided the material foundations of the regional economy across Korea and Japan during the Korean War.
Against the conventional view that illicit exchanges exist outside the formal economy and legal regulations, the book examines how the interlinked markets for transactional sex and goods crucially constituted the transpacific formation of US military base capitalism in post-World War II East Asia. Through innovative archival research, it uncovers the crucial roles that local women played in circulating war supplies and currency across the region.
The result is an intimate and global history of the Korean War that urges us to rethink the often-antithetical relationship between sexual intimacy and market economies in the context of war and occupation.

Join us for the Duke Office of Scientific Integrity's Virtual Research Town Hall, "Beyond advice: Building effective mentor-mentee relationships" on October 27, 2026 from 10:00am - 11:30am.
Effective mentorship plays a critical role in research excellence, career development, and fostering a positive research culture within the research community. Our speakers will explore mentorship as a key component of researcher development, including how mentoring differs from other forms of professional support and how researchers can cultivate meaningful and productive mentoring relationships.

item.title: Live Music at Motorco: Friko with Nine Perfect Lives — Tue Oct 27, 8:00 PM — Motorco
item.description:
Friko will be partnering with Plus1 to collect funds for Santa for a Day! $1 from every ticket sold will go to Santa for a Day, a certified 501 (c) (3) Public Charity who answers letters to Santa from kids in underserved communities. This two-pronged literacy component is vital to their mission: Volunteers helping, teaching youngsters the power of the pen… and then donors rewarding their efforts, by translating their wishes into reality, This process helps children feel seen, heard, and valued—often for the first time—while fostering family dignity and empowerment that extends well beyond the holidays as participants author a different, more positive narrative about life, one sparked by optimism and the vision of a brighter future. Founded in 2018, SFAD has fulfilled more than 50,000 letters and delivered nearly 100,000 gifts to children across eight U.S. cities.

item.description: Congratulations! Your body has developed a tail. We have absolutely no idea how this happened. You provide the willingness to grow something weird. No experience necessary. You’ll learn how to shape, sew and stuff your tail, then install the LED system and bring your new appendage to life. Your finished tail has multiple animated lighting modes, so you can switch up your glow depending on your mood, your outfit, or whatever mysterious creature you have decided to become. And yes, you get to take your new body modification home. Your new tail is perfect for your next Halloween costume, rave, or just being dramatically more interesting than anyone else. • Minimum age: 16. • No experience needed. • Approximate time: 1–1.5 hours. • 6 people per session. • $50 workshop fee + tax includes all materials and tools.

item.title: Dueling Dinosaurs Sensory Friendly Mornings — Sun Nov 8, 10:00 AM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
Explore the Dueling Dinosaurs exhibit with reduced noise effects and smaller crowds. Please bring any noise-reducing headphones and fidgets you may need! A limited number of Sensory Friendly Bags are available for checkout at the front desk, and a limited number of noise-reducing headphones are available to borrow at the exhibit. Free registration is not necessary but encouraged; if you register, we’ll send reminder emails and resources about the exhibit so you can know before you go! Please note that this is a self-guided tour of the exhibit space (not led by a museum educator), though you may interact with the research team in the SECU DinoLab! Register Now!
Recommended Audience All ages, particularly neurodivergent audiences. Children must be accompanied by adults.
Questions? If you have any questions, please contact the Coordinator of Accessibility, Sam Frigerio, at Accessibility@NaturalSciences.org or 919.707.9824.
